title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues the setup of the previous page. There Grothendieck fixed a standard model π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1_C − {0,1,∞}, P^+) = ⟨ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ | ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = 1⟩. This free group of rank 2 sits inside an orbifold group π̃_{0,3} = ⟨ρ, σ_∞ | ρ^3 = σ_∞^2 = 1⟩ ≅ PSL(2,Z), the group of the S_3-quotient of M_{0,3}. It also sits inside the extension by complex conjugation σ̃_∞, giving the extended modular group GL(2,Z)/±1. In modular terms π_{0,3} is Γ(2)/±1, a normal subgroup of index 6 with quotient S_3.

(33), first block. Grothendieck defines ε_0 = σ_∞ρ, a product of an order-2 and an order-3 element. This is a parabolic element (the T-type generator of PSL(2,Z)). He sets ε_1 = ρε_0ρ^{-1} and ε_∞ = ρ^2ε_0ρ^{-2}, and puts ℓ_i = ε_i^2. These are the familiar facts that T^2 generates the cusp stabilizer in Γ(2), and that the ε_i are 'half-loops' around the three cusps. Then ρ permutes the indices cyclically, 0→1→∞→0, on both ε_i and ℓ_i. One checks directly that ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = ρ^3 = 1, so this is consistent.

(33), second block. τ_∞ = σ_∞σ̃_∞ is an involution; it is complex conjugation with a real base point between 0 and 1. The explicit actions on generators, using ℓ_∞ = ℓ_0^{-1}ℓ_1^{-1}, are:
- σ_∞ swaps ℓ_0 and ℓ_1, and sends ℓ_∞ to ℓ_1^{-1}ℓ_0^{-1} = Int(ℓ_0)(ℓ_∞).
- σ̃_∞ sends ℓ_0 → ℓ_1^{-1}, ℓ_1 → ℓ_0^{-1} and ℓ_∞ → ℓ_∞^{-1}.
- τ_∞ sends ℓ_0 → ℓ_0^{-1}, ℓ_1 → ℓ_1^{-1} and ℓ_∞ → ℓ_0ℓ_1 = Int(ℓ_0)(ℓ_∞^{-1}).
Composing σ_∞ and σ̃_∞ in either order gives these same values, so they commute as automorphisms.

Second half: 'pinning' (épinglage). The surface Σ̃ carries a combinatorial decomposition with vertex-like data i ∈ I, ω, ϖ and edges ε = ω∧ϖ. A frame is an element r = (i, ω, ϖ) of Rep(I, ϖ) ≅ I × ω × ϖ. To each frame Grothendieck attaches isomorphisms ψ_ε^{i,ω}: π_{0,3} → Π_ε and ψ_i^{ω,ε}: π_{0,3} → Π_i. These are compatible with the base-change isomorphisms φ_{iε}, φ_{εi} between Π_i and Π_ε (the commutative triangle (35)).

The next page realizes these by transport of structure. One uses the unique conformal isomorphism U_{0,3} → a piece of Σ̃ that sends the standard frame {∞, 0, 1} to the frame (i, ω, ε). He then counts the choices (6, then 4, then 3) under the S_3 and conjugation symmetries.

Purpose: rigidified bookkeeping of local fundamental groups (Lego pieces of type (0,3)), so that the Galois / GT action on Teichmüller groups can be computed formally in a fixed standard group.
errors: Grothendieck writes Π̃_{0,3} ≃ Sl(2,Z). The holomorphic part ⟨ρ, σ_∞⟩ is PSL(2,Z), and with σ̃_∞ one gets GL(2,Z)/±1, as the previous page itself states. This is a notational slip, not a mathematical error.
No substantive errors. The formulas for σ_∞, σ̃_∞ and τ_∞ on ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ check out, as do ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = 1 and the commutation σ_∞σ̃_∞ = σ̃_∞σ_∞ (as automorphisms of π_{0,3}).

ideas.what: Free group π_{0,3} = Γ(2)/±1 inside the orbifold group PSL(2,Z) = ⟨ρ, σ | ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1⟩, with half-loops ε_i = cusp parabolics whose squares are the loops ℓ_i, and ρ permuting the cusps cyclically
ideas.modern_name: Γ(2) ⊂ PSL(2,Z); S_3-symmetry of P^1 − {0,1,∞}; parabolic generators
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke); used in GT theory by Drinfeld, Ihara
ideas.where_published: The S_3 and complex-conjugation symmetry of the (0,3) Lego piece is alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme; these explicit formulas are not published there

ideas.what: Extension by complex conjugation (σ̃_∞, τ_∞) acting on the generators by inversion/permutation
ideas.modern_name: extended modular group GL(2,Z)/±1; action of complex conjugation on π_1 of the projective line minus three points
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; in GT context Drinfeld/Ihara, Lochak–Schneps

ideas.what: Pinning isomorphisms from the standard π_{0,3} to local groups Π_ε, Π_i, indexed by frames (i, ω, ϖ), forming a commutative triangle with the base-change isomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: rigidification / tangential base points for Lego pieces of pants decompositions; base-point groupoid bookkeeping
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (1990s) for Teichmüller Lego / GT action

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful, correct bookkeeping: standard PSL(2,Z)/Γ(2) formulas plus conjugation actions, and a scheme of pinning isomorphisms for (0,3)-pieces. It is an interesting witness of how Grothendieck set up the Lego formalism, but the content is routine and corresponds to standard later practice.
transcription_corrections: τ_∞(ℓ_∞) should read ℓ_0ℓ_1 = Int(ℓ_0)(ℓ_∞^{-1}). The struck-through fragment is the Int(ℓ_0) notation, written as (ℓ_0)(ℓ_∞^{-1}).
σ_∞(ℓ_∞) = ℓ_1^{-1}ℓ_0^{-1} = Int(ℓ_0)(ℓ_∞). The struck symbol before (ℓ_0)(ℓ_∞) is 'Int'.
ε_0 = σ_∞ρ. The trailing '_ε [?]' after ρ appears to be a scribble, not an index.
The ψ in (34) carry crossed-out indices; the margin note reads 'isoms dits d'épinglage'.
